case_title: Prem Kumar Gulati v. State of Haryana
accused_occupation: Worked at a flour mill (per his own defence statement)
previous_criminal_record: Not stated (an earlier 2001 criminal complaint was compromised; no conviction recorded)
accused_victim_relationship: Spouse (husband Mahender Singh); brother-in-law Prem Kumar Gulati; alleged prior disputes over harassment and the husband's illicit relationship with the brother-in-law's wife
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 r/w s.34; IPC s.498A r/w s.34
evidence_type: Dying declaration (primary); medical evidence (post-mortem and medico-legal); father's and brother's testimony on harassment and prior disputes; investigation/site evidence; defence child witness
trial_court_outcome: Convicted all three accused under s.302/498A r/w s.34 IPC; life imprisonment and fine of Rs.5,000 under s.302, one year RI and fine of Rs.500 under s.498A (each accused)
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; trial court judgment upheld (the header of the HC order gives 09.05.2008 while the text gives 06.09.2008)
offence_finally_established: For main accused Mahender Singh: murder (IPC s.302 r/w s.34) and cruelty (IPC s.498A r/w s.34) upheld. Prem Kumar Gulati acquitted of both.
neutral_facts: The victim, a 28-year-old married woman, was admitted to hospital with extensive burn injuries on the night of 9 December 2003, after kerosene oil was poured on her at her matrimonial home and set alight. Burns covered roughly half her body. Once a doctor certified her fit to give a statement, a Magistrate recorded her statement. She said that at about 9.30 to 10.00 p.m. the accused, a husband, a brother-in-law and the brother-in-law's wife, had poured kerosene oil on her and set her ablaze, and that nobody tried to extinguish the fire. She said the husband had an illicit relationship with the brother-in-law's wife, that she quarrelled with him over it, and that after drinking liquor he beat her with a stick and shoes. Investigators inspected the scene, seized burnt clothing, ash and a kerosene lamp, and obtained post-mortem and forensic reports. The post-mortem doctor attributed death to ante-mortem burns sufficient to cause death in the ordinary course of nature. A medical examiner noted superficial deep burns across the body and said burns from kerosene falling on the head could not be ruled out. The victim's father testified to dowry harassment, earlier divorce proceedings, panchayat settlements and a telephone call a week before the incident seeking to return to her parents' home. The victim's brother supported this account. No eyewitness saw the incident. The defence case was that the burns were accidental, caused by a lamp falling on the victim in the kitchen, and it relied on the testimony of the victim's eight-year-old daughter. Investigators found the brother-in-law and his wife living separately and recorded no specific act by either of them.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from about 50% ante-mortem burns; superficial deep burns all over the body
number_of_offences: 2 charged (s.302 r/w s.34 IPC; s.498A r/w s.34 IPC); 2 finally upheld for main accused Mahender Singh
motive: alleged: husband's illicit relationship with the brother-in-law's wife and dowry-related harassment; the court did not separately decide the motive
key_evidence_accepted: Dying declaration (found truthful and reliable) and other evidence establishing that the main accused instigated and caused the burning; the dying declaration was not discarded merely for lacking a question-answer form
witness_credibility: The court accepted the dying declaration's reliability and upheld the main accused's conviction. It found the evidence insufficient to link the brother-in-law and his wife to any specific act, and it did not separately assess the defence child witness.
trial_duration: offence: 09.12.2003; trial judgment: 25.04.2006; High Court: 06.09.2008 (header gives 09.05.2008); Supreme Court: 23.09.2014
legal_representation: Accused: Ms. Meenakshi Arora, Sr. Adv., with Jasbir Singh Malik (for S. K. Sabharwal), Adv. State: Roopansh Purohit, AAG, with Ramesh Kumar, Ms. Naresh Bakshi and Daya Krishan Sharma, Advs.
investigation_status: FIR registered on the basis of the dying declaration; investigation completed; charge sheet against only the main accused; co-accused summoned under s.319 Cr.P.C.; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: Brother-in-law and his wife were not charged by police and were added as accused only through s.319 Cr.P.C. summons
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted all three accused. High Court: appeal dismissed, judgment upheld. Supreme Court: main accused's conviction upheld; brother-in-law acquitted
prosecution_argument: The dying declaration alone suffices; it need not be in question-answer form and narrative form is more natural (citing Shariff); the father's evidence is reliable and the deceased was not influenced by him; the brother-in-law and his wife lived in the same building
defence_argument: Brother-in-law's innocence was found during investigation; dying declaration is vague, lacks time of recording and state of mind, and is not in question-answer form; no eyewitness; child witness wrongly disbelieved; motive from past litigation cannot be ruled out
legal_principle_applied: A truthful and reliable dying declaration can be the sole basis of conviction, subject to close scrutiny; it need not be in question-answer form; benefit of doubt for a co-accused where there is no corroboration and no specific act is attributed to him
precedent_relied_upon: Godhu v. State of Rajasthan (1975) 3 SCC 241; K. Ramachandra Reddy v. Public Prosecutor (1976) 3 SCC 618; Kali Ram v. State of Himachal Pradesh (1973) 2 SCC 808; Khushal Rao v. State of Bombay (AIR 1958 SC 22, quoted); Harbans Singh v. State of Punjab (AIR 1962 SC 439); Tapinder Singh v. State of Punjab (1970) 2 SCC 113; Lallubhai Devchand Shah v. State of Gujarat (1971) 3 SCC 767
other_sentence_order: Brother-in-law Prem Kumar Gulati to be released forthwith; the main accused's appeal dismissed

prosecution_argument.quote: the statement made by the deceased on the dying declaration is sufficient to convict the appellants
